analysis:
Examined the four modified ProviderLoop files. Changes:
(1) ProviderLoop+AppAttestShadow.swift:115/120 and ProviderLoop+AppAttestWorker.swift:10 swap `servingDrain.refusing` for `servingDrain.refusingForServiceChange` in the update-quarantine worker-resume guards. Effect: an add-on hold (new ProviderDrain.Owner .addonHold) no longer blocks worker resume or retry after an update stop. The other guards are unchanged: updatePhase == .idle, !isShuttingDown, and the stop reason being .update. A lifecycle owner is still rejected at AppAttestWorker:6 (owner != .lifecycle). Whether .lifecycle and .update owners still count as refusingForServiceChange depends on the ProviderDrain definition, which was not supplied. If that property excluded the lifecycle or update owner, the worker could resume during a drain. This is a cross-file contract for integration to check, not a demonstrated regression.
(2) ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift:11-14 skips the lifecycleStatus overwrite for the .addonHold owner. Line 146 adds a new mailbox consumer, acceptPendingAddonControl(from:), to the lifecycle monitor loop. Its implementation, the mailbox claim path and request validation are not in the supplied evidence. The next pass should confirm it uses the same ProcessIdentity-bound isValid(for:) check as the drain and switch requests (TB-003 local operator boundary). It should also confirm a local process cannot use it to unload models or deny service beyond what the existing lifecycle mailbox permits (T-016, TB-003).
(3) ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift:1189-1191 skips persistLoadedModelSet during an add-on hold's temporary unload, so the persisted serving set is kept. This is availability-neutral and has no confidentiality impact.
App Attest proof verification, the custody decryption with the process X25519 key (A-003), the coordinator authorization binding (T-053), and the lifecycle `drainAndShutdown` worker-stop path (`stopAppAttestWorkerAndWait`) are untouched. No finding is raised. needs_deeper_review is set because ProviderDrain (refusingForServiceChange, .addonHold) and acceptPendingAddonControl are outside the supplied evidence.
